title: The Road Home
audience: North Indian families and a phone-first festival audience; a one-minute portrait reel explaining why Diwali is celebrated
notes: Portrait 9:16 test film. The question is why Diwali is celebrated in North India. Facts: Diwali is the festival of lights, a row of clay lamps (diyas); in North India it remembers Rama's return to Ayodhya with Sita and Lakshmana after fourteen years of exile and the defeat of Ravana; the people lit lamps to welcome them home. It is also the night Lakshmi is welcomed, and the five-day sequence is Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi/Chhoti Diwali, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj. The film says the regional story plainly and does not claim every family tells it the same way. Public sources checked: Britannica, Diwali; Wikipedia, Diwali; National Geographic Kids, Diwali; Chotteylal and Sons, five days of Diwali. No invented date, city, person, family, price or political claim. The village/Ayodhya is a paper evocation, not a historical reconstruction.
